rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the key uncertainty is the performance floor for the simplest RNA-only baseline. This experiment tests a minimal single-profile RNA PCA pipeline with no aggregation or fusion, providing a clean reference point. It is the best first use of budget because it is simple, low-cost, and will help interpret later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation, image-only performance, and multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline with moderate performance (accuracy 0.485, F1 0.464), leaving major uncertainty about whether the image modality contributes useful signal. This experiment tests an image-only single-profile ResNet50 model, establishing the simplest strong image baseline. It is the best next use of budget because it avoids jumping to multimodal fusion or changing multiple RNA design choices, while directly informing whether image features are competitive and whether multimodal experiments are likely to be worthwhile.

RNA-only PCA is currently much stronger than image-only ResNet, but only one RNA encoder has been tested. This experiment tests whether a learned RNA representation (scvi_n200) improves over PCA while keeping model setting, profile setting, and aggregation fixed, cleanly isolating the effect of representation. That information is important before adding multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion, because it will determine whether later experiments should build on PCA or a learned RNA encoder.

RNA-only singleprofile models currently outperform image-only, and scvi_n200 is better than pca_n2000, but the evidence is still sparse. config_007 tests scgpt under the same singleprofile setting, isolating the effect of RNA representation from profile and aggregation changes. This is the best next experiment because it clarifies whether another RNA encoder can improve the current best RNA-only baseline before spending budget on multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models outperform image-only resnet50, and scvi_n200 is the strongest tested RNA encoder in singleprofile settings, with validation accuracy 0.5203 and F1 0.4982. This experiment tests whether the best RNA representation improves when using multiprofile data with the simplest aggregation, avgpool, compared with the singleprofile scvi_n200 baseline. It is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest current evidence while reducing uncertainty about profile setting and aggregation before moving to more complex choices such as transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models outperform image-only models, scvi_n200 is the strongest RNA encoder, and multiprofile with avgpool gives the largest validated gain so far (config_005: 0.650 acc / 0.628 F1). The main uncertainty is whether a stronger aggregation method can further improve this promising RNA multiprofile setup. config_006 tests transformer aggregation while keeping the same rna_only, multiprofile, and scvi_n200 setting as config_005, isolating the effect of aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it directly extends the strongest observed direction, is highly informative, and avoids changing multiple design choices at once.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA modeling with scvi_n200 improves validation accuracy from 0.520 single-profile to about 0.650 multiprofile, with avgpool and transformer aggregation nearly tied. The key uncertainty is whether this multiprofile gain is a general property of the profile setting or specific to the scvi representation. Testing pca_n2000 with multiprofile and simple avgpool directly compares against the single-profile pca baseline and the scvi multiprofile results, helping isolate the effect of profile setting before adding image or fusion complexity. This is a lower-complexity, high-information experiment under a limited budget.

Multiprofile RNA is clearly stronger than single-profile RNA, and scvi_n200 multiprofile is the current best, but the transformer-vs-avgpool difference is small in both accuracy and F1. The cleanest missing comparison in the current RNA multiprofile grid is pca_n2000 with transformer aggregation, directly comparable to config_002. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation generally improves multiprofile RNA or is specific to scvi_n200, without confounding from image modality or fusion. Under a limited budget, it is the most efficient next step because it isolates an important design choice, avoids overinterpreting a tiny performance gap, and solidifies the strongest unimodal direction before adding multimodal complexity.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and simple aggregation are much better than singleprofile RNA or image-only baselines, with avgpool and transformer nearly tied. This experiment keeps that promising RNA setting fixed and adds a simple concat fusion with the already-tested resnet50 image encoder, directly testing whether image information improves on the best RNA-only baseline. It is a minimal, high-value extension: if it helps, multimodal fusion is worth further exploration; if not, it shows resnet/concat fusion is not adding value before trying weighted fusion or stronger image encoders.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is the strongest evidence so far (≈0.653 acc/0.628 F1), while the only multimodal test with ResNet50, avgpool, and concat is slightly below it (0.6315 acc/0.6068 F1), leaving uncertainty about whether the image modality can help or whether concat fusion is the bottleneck. config_031 changes only fusion to weighted, holding RNA encoder, profile setting, image encoder, and aggregation fixed, so it directly tests whether adaptive fusion can make the multimodal model competitive. This one-factor extension of the existing multimodal result is the most efficient next use of budget before moving to new image encoders or aggregation choices.
